LanguageData.AAI_Enabled_Desc: Off: nobody uses abilities through this mod; vanilla's or their own mod's casting takes over.
LanguageData.AAI_Enabled_Tip: Raiders, visitors, animals and mechs decide for themselves when to use abilities that are set up for this mod, and your own pawns use the abilities you set to autocast. Off: nobody does, and abilities fall back to whatever casting vanilla or their own mod gives them.
LanguageData.AAI_Hostiles_Tip: Raiders and anyone else hostile to your colony.
LanguageData.AAI_NonHostiles_Tip: Visitors, traders, caravan guards and allied soldiers.
LanguageData.AAI_Animals_Tip: Wild animals and other factions' animals. Yours use the abilities you set to autocast; one that can't be drafted only does so with "Also while undrafted" on.
LanguageData.AAI_Mechs_Tip: Other factions' mechanoids. Yours use the abilities you set to autocast.
LanguageData.AAI_Who_Desc: Your own colonists, slaves, ghouls and mechs only use abilities you set to autocast. Prisoners never use any.
LanguageData.AAI_Unclaimed: Also use abilities no mod claims
LanguageData.AAI_Unclaimed_Desc: Such as a raider psycaster's own psycasts. Rules marked off for NPCs stay off.
LanguageData.AAI_Unclaimed_Tip: Mods built on Ability AI (such as Entad Framework and Bastle Framework) claim the abilities their own gear and traits give. With this on, a pawn also uses any other ability that is set up for this mod, such as a raider psycaster's own psycasts (most combat psycasts from Royalty and Vanilla Psycasts Expanded are). Off: only claimed abilities.
LanguageData.AAI_VanillaStandDown: Replace vanilla's casting for abilities this mod handles
LanguageData.AAI_VanillaStandDown_Tip: Some abilities also have vanilla's simple casting turned on, so they still get used when this mod is missing, and Vanilla Expanded Framework casts its abilities for NPCs at random in place of an attack. With this on, both stay out of the way of any ability Ability AI is deciding for, so two AIs never use the same ability. Off: both may cast it.
LanguageData.AAI_Approach: Walk into range to use an ability
LanguageData.AAI_Approach_Tip: A ranged raider, visitor, animal or mech in a fight walks a few tiles closer when a target for one of its abilities is just out of range or out of sight, uses it, and then fights as usual. Only for abilities set up for it, such as flashbang and battle cry. Never while badly hurt, fleeing or held in melee. This setting doesn't cover your own pawns: they walk only for abilities you set to "Full Autocast", whether this is on or off.
LanguageData.AAI_PlayerAutocast_Tip: Right-click an ability button to choose whether your pawn uses it by itself. Only for abilities the AI knows how to use. Drafted, the pawn casts while it stands in position or shoots, never in the middle of a move you ordered (a melee attack order excepted, see below). With "Full Autocast" a drafted ranged pawn also walks a few tiles to get a target in range, casts, and walks back to where it stood or finds new cover (see below); any order you give in the meantime cancels the walk back.
LanguageData.AAI_UndraftedAutocast_Tip: Lets undrafted pawns autocast too. Any time: abilities that aren't only for fighting (recovering a low need, helping a downed ally, calming an ally in a mental break, putting out fires). While fleeing: movement abilities as well. While fighting back (a colonist with its hostility response set to attack, or an animal defending itself or released on an enemy, that is attacking or was hit in the last 10 seconds): every ability. The pawn stops its current job to cast, but never while lying down, carrying something, doing a job you ordered, or doing a job that can't be interrupted (surgery, bills). An attack it was making is picked up again after the cast. A pawn whose hostility response is attack or flee checks for an ability before attacking or running, so it can, for example, calm a berserk friend instead of fighting it.
LanguageData.AAI_UndraftedInterval: Check undrafted pawns every {0} ticks ({1} s)
LanguageData.AAI_UndraftedInterval_Tip: How often an undrafted pawn that isn't fighting back or fleeing looks for something to autocast. Higher is cheaper on large colonies; lower reacts sooner to a downed ally or a low need. Drafted pawns, pawns fighting back or fleeing, and other factions' pawns are always checked every 30 ticks (0.5 s), and drafting a pawn or a fight starting cuts the wait short. Default 250 (about 4 s).
LanguageData.AAI_BlockedJobs_Tip: Pick the jobs an undrafted pawn finishes before it autocasts: by default meals, recreation, gatherings, rituals and childcare.
LanguageData.AAI_BlockedJobs_Desc: An undrafted pawn doing a checked job won't stop it to autocast ({0} checked). Jobs you ordered, jobs that can't be interrupted (surgery, bills, lovin'), lying down and carrying something are always left alone and aren't listed. Drafted pawns ignore this list.
LanguageData.AAI_BlockedJobs_GroupOff: Other jobs that can be interrupted
LanguageData.AAI_ChargeGapClose: Leap at the target of a melee attack order
LanguageData.AAI_ChargeGapClose_Tip: When you order a drafted pawn to attack someone in melee, it may use a movement ability set to autocast (Power Leap, Blink, Shadowskip, Ghostwalk) to close the distance, then carries on with the attack. Only while the target is further away than the ability's minimum, and only movement abilities: nothing else is cast during the charge, and the pawn never uses one to run away from the fight you ordered.
LanguageData.AAI_ShowMarker_Tip: Draws a small grey ring on the button of every ability your pawn could autocast but isn't set to.
LanguageData.AAI_AutocastOwner: With Better Autocasting also installed, priority is given to:
LanguageData.AAI_AutocastOwner_Tip: Better Autocasting for Vanilla Psycasts Expanded has its own autocast for about forty VPE psycasts. Where Ability AI also has rules for one (Overshield, Word of Serenity, ...), only one of the two mods casts it for your colonists, and its gizmo has one autocast toggle. Switching keeps each colonist's on or off choice. Mechs, animals and NPCs always use Ability AI's rules.
LanguageData.AAI_AutocastOwner_AbilityAI_Tip: Right-click menu with Autocast and Full Autocast, Ability AI's targeting and your psycast limits. Better Autocasting's settings for these psycasts have no effect.
LanguageData.AAI_AutocastOwner_BetterAutocast_Tip: VEF's autocast toggle and Better Autocasting's own targeting settings. Ability AI leaves these psycasts alone for colonists.
LanguageData.AAI_ReturnTo: After moving to cast an ability:
LanguageData.AAI_ReturnTo_Tip: Where a drafted pawn goes after moving to cast an ability set to "Full Autocast".
LanguageData.AAI_ReturnTo_Original_Tip: The pawn walks back to the exact spot it was standing on before it set off.
LanguageData.AAI_ReturnTo_Cover: Find new cover from the ending position
LanguageData.AAI_ReturnTo_Cover_Tip: The pawn looks for a spot within 6 tiles of where it ended up that has cover from the nearest enemy and that it can shoot from, and goes there. It stays put if its own spot already has good cover. If there is none, it walks back to its original position.
LanguageData.AAI_CalmBreaks: Your pawns will use calming abilities on:
LanguageData.AAI_CalmBreaks_Tip: Which of an ally's mental breaks your pawns end by themselves with an ability set to autocast. Word of serenity also puts the target into a psychic coma for a few hours and costs more psyfocus for a worse break (30% minor, 50% major, 70% extreme). Breaks that will end on their own within a minute are left alone. Raiders and visitors only ever calm aggressive breaks.
LanguageData.AAI_CalmBreaks_Aggressive_Tip: Berserk, murderous rage and other breaks where the pawn attacks people.
LanguageData.AAI_CalmBreaks_Major_Tip: Aggressive breaks, plus major and extreme ones such as psychotic wandering, tantrums, fire starting and catatonic breakdown. Minor breaks such as sad wandering, a food binge or hiding in a room are left to run.
LanguageData.AAI_CalmBreaks_Any_Tip: Every mental break, minor ones included.
LanguageData.AAI_CalmRange: Undrafted, walk up to {0} tiles to calm someone
LanguageData.AAI_CalmRange_Tip: Measured in a straight line, so the walk itself can be longer. How far an undrafted pawn goes to use a calming ability it has to touch the target with. Drafted pawns keep the ability's own reach (8 tiles for word of serenity), so they don't walk far from where you put them.
LanguageData.AAI_BreakCasting: Your pawns use abilities during mental breaks
LanguageData.AAI_BreakCasting_Tip: A pawn of yours in a mental break (a colonist, or an animal gone manhunter) is out of your control, so your autocast choices don't apply. With this on, a pawn in an aggressive break uses its abilities the way a raider would, treating your other pawns as enemies, and a panicking one may use movement abilities to flee. Off: the game's own AI decides, as it would without this mod.
LanguageData.AAI_BrokenAllies: Hostile abilities on allies in a break
LanguageData.AAI_BrokenAllies_Tip: A berserk colonist or a tame animal gone manhunter attacks its own side. This decides whether its friends use their enemy abilities on it. It applies to every caster: your pawns on autocast, raiders and visitors alike. Calming abilities are not affected; they have their own setting.
LanguageData.AAI_BrokenAllies_Never_Tip: Allies in a break are treated as friends: never targeted, and kept out of area abilities that avoid allies.
LanguageData.AAI_BrokenAllies_Harmless_Tip: Only abilities that disable without lasting harm, such as stun, burden and blinding pulse. Everything else treats them as friends.
LanguageData.AAI_BrokenAllies_Any_Tip: Allies in a break are treated as enemies, damaging abilities included.
LanguageData.AAI_Limits_Heat_Tip: Autocast won't use a psycast that would push this pawn's neural heat past this point. All the way right: no limit beyond the game's own heat limit. Casting by hand ignores this.
LanguageData.AAI_Limits_Focus_Tip: Autocast won't use a psycast that would bring this pawn's psyfocus below this point. Casting by hand ignores this.
LanguageData.AAI_MinGap: Least time between one pawn's casts: {0} s
LanguageData.AAI_MinGap_Desc: Stops a pawn with several abilities from using them all in the same moment. Each ability's own cooldown and charges still apply.
LanguageData.AAI_SkipRepel: Skip enemies away from allies who can't fight them off
LanguageData.AAI_SkipRepel_Tip: An enemy standing next to a downed or badly hurt ally, or next to someone with a ranged weapon, is skipped far from the caster's side and back toward its own. Never into your home area when the caster is yours or friendly to you. Healthy melee fighters are left to their fight.
LanguageData.AAI_SkipRescue: Skip downed or badly hurt allies out of danger
LanguageData.AAI_SkipRescue_Tip: A downed ally with an enemy within 10 tiles, or a badly hurt ally being hit or shot at, is skipped to a spot near the caster, away from the enemies and behind cover if there is any. Drafted pawns on their feet and pawns doing something you ordered stay where they are.
LanguageData.AAI_SkipEscape: Skip the caster away when it is in trouble
LanguageData.AAI_SkipEscape_Tip: When the caster is badly hurt, fleeing, or has a ranged weapon and is caught in melee, it skips itself to the spot furthest from every enemy within reach.
LanguageData.AAI_Skip_Desc: For every pawn that uses Skip on its own: yours set to autocast it, and other factions' psycasters.
LanguageData.AAI_CaiHoldNpcs: Other factions' casts can't be cut off by CAI
LanguageData.AAI_CaiHoldNpcs_Tip: CAI 5000 sends pawns under fire to cover, to duck or to retreat, and that cancels a psycast's warmup. With this on, CAI waits until the cast has gone off (and until a channelled effect such as Frost Ray's ray has ended, up to 10 seconds) before it moves the pawn. With it off, CAI reacts as it would without Ability AI.
LanguageData.AAI_CaiHoldColonists: Your auto-controlled pawns' casts can't be cut off by CAI
LanguageData.AAI_CaiHoldColonists_Tip: The same for your drafted colonists and mechs that you have handed to CAI's auto-control. CAI never moves your pawns that aren't on auto-control, so this doesn't affect them.
LanguageData.AAI_Cai_Desc: Switch off to compare how pawns fight when CAI may interrupt their casts.
LanguageData.AAI_DebugLog_Tip: Writes a line to the log each time a pawn decides to cast something, naming the rule it used. When a pawn with abilities set up for this mod checks and casts nothing, it also writes why, at most once every 10 seconds per pawn.
LanguageData.AAI_Reset_Confirm: Reset every Ability AI setting, on every tab, to its default?
